alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{Actor}} performed {{OperationName}} against {{TargetUser}}, an administrative password reset on another account.

properties.query:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName has_any ("Reset user password", "Reset password", "Change user password")
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend Actor = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend TargetUser = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(Actor) and isnotempty(TargetUser)
| where tolower(Actor) != tolower(TargetUser)
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, TargetUser, OperationName, CorrelationId
| extend Account = TargetUser
properties.displayName: Entra - Password Reset Performed on Another User
properties.description:
DETECTS
An administrative password reset where the actor and the target are different accounts. Self-service resets are excluded.

WHY IT MATTERS
Resetting another user password is a direct account takeover primitive. An attacker holding User Administrator or Helpdesk Administrator uses it to seize a more privileged identity, and the action looks entirely routine against a backdrop of legitimate helpdesk work (MITRE T1098, Account Manipulation). Resets targeting privileged accounts are the ones that matter.

TRIAGE
1. Determine the target account privilege level. A reset against an administrator is significantly more serious.
2. Confirm a corresponding helpdesk ticket exists.
3. Verify the actor is in a helpdesk or identity administration role.
4. Check whether the target account signed in from an unusual location shortly after the reset.
5. If unauthorized: reset the target password again through a verified channel, revoke sessions, and investigate the actor.

FALSE POSITIVES
Routine helpdesk operations, which will dominate the volume. This rule is most useful when scoped to resets targeting privileged accounts.

SOURCE
AuditLogs
